theorem_Q2_implies_Q1.proof: Q2(r) asserts existence of b satisfying TargetA(b) AND CompletionCompatible(b), a conjunction. Any witness for the conjunction is a witness for its first conjunct alone, which is exactly Q1(r)'s existential statement. No engine computation is needed for this direction; it follows from the predicates' own logical form.
theorem_Q2_implies_Q1.statement: Q2(r) => Q1(r) for every root r

F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible.monotone: not applicable -- it is a structural CONSISTENCY check on the current state, not a forward-looking feasibility test
F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible.monotone_proof: f1_normal_form checks a necessary invariant of every F<=1 reachable prefix (at most one non-current partial hexagon, total fragment components <= F+1); its docstring states this is 'a necessary prefix invariant, not an unproved pruning heuristic'. It references no TARGET_P/TARGET_O/TARGET_D constant.
F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible.reason: does not assume completion; it is a sanity/consistency check on the CURRENT state's geometry. It is expected to be vacuous downstream of F_exceeded (F<=1 states reachable via extend() should always satisfy it), and is kept for defensiveness rather than because it is expected to fire
F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible.target_A_requires: nothing directly, but a state violating this invariant is not a genuinely reachable ExactState under F<=1 at all

F_exceeded.monotone_proof: dF = int(abandonment) in {0,1}; F never decreases along any macro edge
F_exceeded.reason: F_def > 1 can never return to 1 (monotone), and Target A's own recognizer requires the eventual boundary's child to have F_def == 1; so once F_def > 1 no descendant can ever be a Target A boundary
F_exceeded.target_A_requires: the R2-boundary CHILD has F_def == 1 exactly

H_positive.reason: H > 0 can never return to 0 (monotone), and Target A requires the child's H == 0; identical argument to F_exceeded. (Empirically vacuous within the RR alphabet actually explored here, since weight is 2 or 3 for every RR joint and dH = 0 for both -- but the argument does not depend on that, and is recorded for completeness.)
H_positive.target_A_requires: the R2-boundary CHILD has H == 0 exactly

N_exceeded_monotone.monotone_proof: dNdef = dS + dF - dO in {0, +1} for every legal macro edge (dS = [weight>=3], dO = [new orbit], dF = [abandonment]; case analysis over the four RR joints shows dNdef is never negative)
N_exceeded_monotone.reason: monotone, so a valid prune for staying inside Area A. This is a SCOPE restriction, not a completeness claim: a Target A boundary with Ndef > 3 could exist outside Area A and is simply not explored by this search, exactly as it was not explored by any prior round's search either
N_exceeded_monotone.target_A_requires: nothing directly -- n_limit=3 defines AREA A, the disclosed search SCOPE this entire Target A/B corpus has operated within since Round 27 (every one of the 18 known boundaries has a child that passes this test)
N_exceeded_monotone.verdict: Q1-SAFE, WITHIN THE DISCLOSED AREA-A SCOPE

P_exceeded.monotone_proof: P = sum of orbit_masks popcounts, incremented by exactly 1 per legal weight>=2 event; never decreases
P_exceeded.reason: Target A does not require P <= 121 at its boundary; a state with P > 121 could not be part of an eventual full completion, but could still be a genuine local Target A boundary (F_def==1, H==0, same-component) in isolation. Using this as a Q1 prune would silently restrict Q1 to 'boundaries reachable en route to completion', exactly the assumption the round prohibits.
P_exceeded.target_A_requires: nothing -- TARGET_P=121 is the pass-start count of a FULL Area-A NR6 completion, not a Target A condition

final_D_impossible.monotone: empirically an INVARIANT of the whole trajectory from the fixed initial state, verified by direct simulation: (TARGET_D - D + r) mod 5 stays constant (0) over a 4000-step random walk from the identity, because each weight>=2 event changes it by either -5 (new orbit, dD=+4) or 0 (old orbit, dD=-1), both preserving the residue mod 5
final_D_impossible.reason: this is the subtle case: because the residue is an invariant of the entire trajectory (not just monotone), it can never actually change from state to state along a legal walk from the true root -- so classifying it Q1-safe or Q2-only makes no PRACTICAL difference for search correctness here. But the PROPERTY it tests -- reachability of TARGET_D at TARGET_P -- is a completion condition Target A does not require, so it is classified Q2-only on principle, not merely for safety margin
final_D_impossible.target_A_requires: nothing -- it tests reachability of the EXACT pair (TARGET_P, TARGET_D), a full-completion condition
final_D_impossible.test: not exact.arithmetic_D_reachable(state), i.e. (TARGET_D - D + r) is not a multiple of 5 in [0, 5r] where r = TARGET_P - P
